sessions.title: Placement chat
turns: Hola! I'm Tomás. I'm learning German, roughly B1, and I sit the Goethe B2 exam in March.
Nice to meet you, Tomás. March gives us time. Where do you lose the most points?
Cases. Dative or accusative after in, an, auf. I guess every time and I'm wrong half the time.
The two-way prepositions. Rule of thumb: movement towards a place takes accusative, location takes dative.
I know the rule. I just can't do it fast while speaking. I need drills, lots of them.
Then every session gets a quick two-way preposition drill.
Can the examples be about football? I watch every Bundesliga weekend. It's the only vocabulary that sticks.
Of course. Der Ball liegt auf dem Rasen; der Spieler schiesst den Ball in das Tor.

sessions.title: Commute drills
turns: I practise on my bike commute now, 20 minutes each way. Can drills be things I say out loud, no reading?
Yes: I'll give you short spoken patterns you can repeat without looking at the screen.
Like the coach shouting? Geh auf den Flügel! Bleib in der Mitte!
Exactly. Auf den Flügel is movement, accusative; in der Mitte is position, dative.
I got four out of five today. Better than last week.
Good progress. The one you missed was an der Seitenlinie: position, so dative.
Also my writing is fine, my teacher says. Don't waste time on essays.
Noted: speaking first, writing only when you ask for it.

sessions.title: Transfer news
turns: Can we do a reading on transfer news? I want the vocabulary for contracts and clubs.
Sure: der Vertrag, die Ablösesumme, der Wechsel, ausleihen.
Ausleihen is to loan a player out?
Right. Der Verein leiht den Spieler an einen anderen Verein aus.
My Goethe mock speaking score was 68 out of 100. I need 60 to pass, but I want more margin.
That's a pass with some room. We'll keep speaking as the main focus.
And keep drilling the two-way prepositions, they still cost me points in the mock.
They stay in every session until they're automatic.

pins: Tomás is learning German (around B1) and sits the Goethe B2 exam in March.
Tomás mixes up dative and accusative after two-way prepositions (in, an, auf) and wants that drilled every session.
Tomás wants examples built around football: Bundesliga matches, training, transfers.
Tomás practises out loud on a 20-minute bike commute, so his drills should be spoken, with no reading.
Tomás's writing is fine; he wants speaking practice first and essays only on request.
